#!/bin/bash
# Run this on your server to set up the git repository and deployment

set -e

# Configuration
GIT_REPO="/git/server"
WEB_ROOT="/var/www/html"
GIT_USER="${GIT_USER:-git}"

echo "Setting up git server..."

# Create git repository directory if it doesn't exist
sudo mkdir -p "$(dirname "$GIT_REPO")"

# Initialize bare repository
if [ ! -d "$GIT_REPO" ]; then
    sudo git init --bare "$GIT_REPO"
    echo "Created bare repository at $GIT_REPO"
else
    echo "Repository already exists at $GIT_REPO"
fi

# Create web root directory
sudo mkdir -p "$WEB_ROOT"
sudo chmod 755 "$WEB_ROOT"

# Create post-receive hook
POST_RECEIVE_HOOK="$GIT_REPO/hooks/post-receive"
sudo tee "$POST_RECEIVE_HOOK" > /dev/null <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash

# Deploy hook - runs after receiving a push
WEB_ROOT="/var/www/html"
TEMP_CHECKOUT=$(mktemp -d)

# Clone the repository to temporary directory
git clone "$GIT_DIR" "$TEMP_CHECKOUT"

# Remove old files and deploy new ones
sudo rm -rf "$WEB_ROOT"/*
sudo cp -r "$TEMP_CHECKOUT"/* "$WEB_ROOT"/

# Clean up
rm -rf "$TEMP_CHECKOUT"

# Set proper permissions
sudo chown -R www-data:www-data "$WEB_ROOT"
sudo chmod -R 755 "$WEB_ROOT"

echo "Deployment complete!"
EOF

# Make hook executable
sudo chmod +x "$POST_RECEIVE_HOOK"

# Set ownership (adjust git user as needed)
sudo chown -R "$GIT_USER:$GIT_USER" "$GIT_REPO"

echo ""
echo "✓ Git server setup complete!"
echo ""
echo "Clone the repository with:"
echo "  git clone user@server:/git/server my-project"
echo ""
echo "Then push to deploy:"
echo "  git push origin master"
echo ""
echo "Your files will be available at http://server:8080/"

#!/bin/bash
# Install and configure nginx on your server

set -e

echo "Installing nginx..."
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y nginx

echo "Setting up nginx configuration..."

# Backup existing config
sudo cp /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/default /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/default.bak

# Copy the provided nginx config
sudo cp nginx.conf /etc/nginx/sites-available/git-deploy

# Remove default site
sudo rm -f /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/default

# Test configuration
sudo nginx -t

# Start/restart nginx
sudo systemctl restart nginx
sudo systemctl enable nginx

echo "✓ Nginx setup complete!"
echo ""
echo "Nginx is now listening on port 8080"
echo "Files in /var/www/html will be served at http://server:8080/"

#!/bin/bash
# This is the post-receive hook that gets installed in the git repository
# It automatically deploys files when you push to the git server

WEB_ROOT="/var/www/html"
REPO_DIR="/tmp/git-deploy-$$"

# Exit on error
set -e

echo "Deploying files..."

# Clone repository to temporary location
git clone "$GIT_DIR" "$REPO_DIR"

# Ensure web root exists
mkdir -p "$WEB_ROOT"

# Copy all files to web root (you may want to use rsync instead)
cp -r "$REPO_DIR"/* "$WEB_ROOT"/ 2>/dev/null || true

# Ensure .git is not exposed
rm -rf "$WEB_ROOT/.git"

# Clean up temp directory
rm -rf "$REPO_DIR"

# Set permissions (www-data is the nginx/Apache user)
# Note: this may require sudo or passwordless sudo setup
if command -v sudo &> /dev/null; then
    sudo chown -R www-data:www-data "$WEB_ROOT" 2>/dev/null || true
fi

echo "✓ Deployment complete!"
echo "Files available at: http://server:8080/"

# Git Server with Auto-Deploy Setup

This setup allows you to automatically deploy files to a web server by pushing to a git repository.

## Architecture

```
Your Computer          Git Server                Web Server
    │                    │                           │
    │─ git push ────────>│                           │
    │                    │─ post-receive hook ──────>│
    │                    │  (copies files)           │
    │                    │                     /var/www/html
    │                    │                           │
    │                                                │
    └────────── curl http://server:8080 ────────────>│
```

## Server Setup Instructions

### 1. Create Git Repository

```bash
sudo mkdir -p /git
sudo git init --bare /git/server
```

### 2. Create Web Root Directory

```bash
sudo mkdir -p /var/www/html
sudo chmod 755 /var/www/html
```

### 3. Install Web Server (nginx)

```bash
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y nginx
```

Create `/etc/nginx/sites-available/git-deploy`:
```nginx
server {
    listen 8080 default_server;
    listen [::]:8080 default_server;
    server_name _;
    root /var/www/html;
    index index.html index.htm;
    
    location / {
        try_files $uri $uri/ =404;
    }
}
```

Then enable it:
```bash
sudo ln -s /etc/nginx/sites-available/git-deploy /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/git-deploy
sudo rm -f /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/default
sudo systemctl restart nginx
sudo systemctl enable nginx
```

### 4. Set Up Post-Receive Hook

Create `/git/server/hooks/post-receive` with this content:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
WEB_ROOT="/var/www/html"
REPO_DIR="/tmp/git-deploy-$$"
set -e

echo "Deploying files..."

# Clone and deploy
git clone "$GIT_DIR" "$REPO_DIR"
cp -r "$REPO_DIR"/* "$WEB_ROOT"/ 2>/dev/null || true
rm -rf "$REPO_DIR"
rm -rf "$WEB_ROOT/.git"

# Set permissions
sudo chown -R www-data:www-data "$WEB_ROOT" 2>/dev/null || true

echo "✓ Deployment complete!"
```

Make it executable:
```bash
sudo chmod +x /git/server/hooks/post-receive
sudo chown -R git:git /git/server  # Replace 'git' with your server user
```

### 5. Configure Passwordless Sudo (Optional but Recommended)

To avoid password prompts during deployment, configure sudo to allow the git user to run chown without a password:

```bash
sudo visudo
```

Add this line at the end:
```
git ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /bin/chown
```

## Using the Setup

### On Your Computer

Clone the repository:
```bash
git clone user@server:/git/server my-project
cd my-project
```

Create a file:
```bash
echo "hello world" > hello.html
git add hello.html
git commit -m "add hello.html"
git push origin master
```

### Verify Deployment

```bash
curl http://server:8080/hello.html
# Output: hello world
```

## Troubleshooting

**Hook doesn't run?**
- Check hook is executable: `ls -l /git/server/hooks/post-receive`
- Check git user has permission: `ls -ld /git/server`

**Permission denied errors?**
- Ensure `/var/www/html` is owned by www-data: `sudo chown www-data:www-data /var/www/html`
- Ensure git user has read permissions on the repo

**Files not appearing?**
- Check nginx is running: `sudo systemctl status nginx`
- Check nginx is listening on 8080: `sudo netstat -tlnp | grep 8080`
- Check files exist: `ls -la /var/www/html/`

**Can't SSH to git repo?**
- Make sure you've set up SSH keys (you mentioned you'll handle this)
- Test: `ssh user@server`

## Security Notes

- The post-receive hook runs with git user privileges
- Files are deployed to `/var/www/html` and served as-is (no processing)
- Avoid pushing sensitive files (credentials, secrets)
- Consider adding `.gitignore` for files that shouldn't be deployed

## Alternative: Using Systemd User Service

If you want more control, you can also set up a systemd user service instead of relying on sudo:

```bash
# This would require more complex setup, ask if you need this
```
